filing.block_desc: Newborn affected by maternal factors and by complications of pregnancy, labor, and delivery (P00-P04)

encounters.cc: Routine prenatal visit at 10 weeks gestation

lines: Routine prenatal visit at 10 weeks gestation
She reports compliance with her prenatal vitamins and has had an uneventful pregnancy thus far.
- History of intravenous drug use disorder in sustained remission
She has a known history of chronic hepatitis C infection, which was diagnosed 5 years ago during a routine health screening.
She has no known history of hepatitis A or B infection and is unsure of her immunization status.
She reports compliance with her prenatal vitamins
Her past medical history is significant for intravenous drug use, which she discontinued 6 years ago.
She denies any history of jaundice, pruritus, or abdominal pain.
Her vital signs are within normal limits
Laboratory studies from her first trimester are as follows:
- Hepatitis C virus RNA, quantitative: 1,500,000 IU/mL
- Hepatitis B core antibody, total: Negative

encounters.cc: Clear fluid leaking from vagina for 2 hours at 32 weeks gestation

lines: Clear fluid leaking from vagina for 2 hours at 32 weeks gestation
Patient with chronic hepatitis C and IVDU in remission presents at 32 weeks after 10-week visit.
She denies contractions, vaginal bleeding, or recent sexual intercourse.
Pregnancy has been uncomplicated with appropriate prenatal care.
- Susceptibility to hepatitis B virus infection (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- History of intravenous drug use disorder in sustained remission
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 6 years ago.
On examination, her vital signs are stable: blood pressure 120/75 mmHg, heart rate 80 bpm, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, and temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F).
Speculum examination confirms pooling of clear fluid in the posterior fornix.
Nitrazine test is positive, and ferning is observed under the microscope.
Fetal heart tracing is reassuring with a baseline of 140 bpm, moderate variability, no decelerations, and no contractions.
C-reactive protein is within normal limits.
The patient is admitted for observation.

encounters.cc: Severe itching of palms and soles for 2 weeks at 35 weeks gestation

lines: Severe itching of palms and soles for 2 weeks at 35 weeks gestation
This 30-year-old with chronic hepatitis C, intravenous drug use in remission, and prior PPROM presents at 35 weeks with pruritus.
She reports the itching is most intense on the palms of her hands and soles of her feet and occurs mostly at night.
She denies rash, jaundice, nausea, vomiting, or change in bowel habits.
- Susceptibility to hepatitis B virus infection (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- History of intravenous drug use disorder in sustained remission
Her pregnancy has been uncomplicated until now.
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 6 years ago.
On examination, there are no skin lesions or rashes noted, and her abdomen is appropriately sized for gestational age with normal fetal heart tones.

encounters.cc: Sudden severe abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding at 34 weeks gestation

lines: Sudden severe abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding at 34 weeks gestation

The patient with chronic hepatitis C, intravenous drug use disorder in sustained remission, and prior preterm premature rupture of membranes and acute fatty liver of pregnancy presents with sharp constant pain rated 8 of 10 severity.
She denies trauma or recent intercourse.
Prenatal course was complicated by severe polyhydramnios.
- Susceptibility to hepatitis B virus infection (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- History of intravenous drug use disorder in sustained remission
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 6 years ago.
Blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, heart rate is 110 bpm
On examination, the uterus is tender to palpation with frequent contractions.
Fetal heart rate monitoring shows a repetitive late deceleration pattern.
- Activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT): 30 seconds (control 25-35 seconds)

encounters.cc: Sudden severe abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, and decreased fetal movement at 39 weeks gestation

lines: Sudden severe abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, and decreased fetal movement at 39 weeks gestation
This patient with chronic hepatitis C, remote IVDU, and prior abruption presents to the labor and delivery unit with 1-hour history of sudden onset of severe abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding.
She reports that the baby has been moving less than usual.
- Susceptibility to hepatitis B virus infection (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- History of intravenous drug use disorder in sustained remission
Her pregnancy has been uncomplicated until now, and she has had appropriate prenatal care.
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 6 years ago.
Her blood pressure is 120/75 mmHg, heart rate is 88 bpm, and temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F).
On examination, her abdomen is tender to palpation in the uterine area, and the uterus is hypertonic.
There are no signs of placental abruption on ultrasound.
Fetal heart monitoring shows recurrent late decelerations, minimal variability, and no accelerations after a 10-minute observation period.
The patient is given oxygen by face mask, IV fluids are started, and she is placed in the left lateral decubitus position.
Despite these measures, the fetal heart tracing does not improve.
